newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber edges up, govt denies China talks.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber edges up, govt denies China talks.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were steady to higher in moderate buying from China and Japan, trade sources said on Wednesday.
They noted market talk that China would buy rubber from Thailand soon but a senior agriculture ministry denied the rumour.
"The negotiation was on and off. But we have no plan to unwind our stock at the moment," an official at the Rubber Research Institute told Reuters.
"If we sold now we would lose money. It is still our policy not to sell at a loss and we won't sell when the market is still on a downtrend as it could pressure prices further," he said.
The official said the government has so far bought 33,000 tonnes of rubber from rubber producers from May 14-July 11 under the intervention scheme.
However, some traders were sceptical about the denial.
"The prime minister said there will be no devaluation and you see what happened to the baht two days later," said one Bangkok trader.
Despite the slight improvement in prices, most players were still bearish.
"China bought 30,000 tonnes of Thai rubber in the past two weeks but that barely lifted the prices," one trader said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for September/October was quoted around 96 US cents per kg FOB Bangkok and December was around 98-99 cents.
